creator: Qian Cai, Hangsai Wang, Yue Zhang, Liuqing Wang, Le Zhao, Xinfen Xu
description: IntroductionThe global burden of cancer is escalating, with Asia accounting for over half of cancer-related deaths worldwide. As cancer often diminishes patients’ quality of life and sense of dignity, dignity-related interventions have gained prominence in palliative care for patients with cancer.

title: Dynamics of a jointly commensurate moiré charge density wave
creator: Kyoung Hun Oh, Yifan Su, Honglie Ning, B. Q. Lv, Alfred Zong, Dong Wu, Qiaomei Liu, Gyeongbo Kang, Hyeongi Choi, Hyun-Woo J. Kim, Seunghyeok Ha, Jaehwon Kim, Suchismita Sarker, Jacob P. C. Ruff, Xiaozhe Shen, Duan Luo, Stephen Weathersby, Patrick Kramer, Xinxin Cheng, Dongsung Choi, Doron Azoury, Ma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The advent of two-dimensional moiré systems has revolutionized the exploration of phenomena arising from strong correlations and nontrivial band topology. Recently, a moiré superstructure formed by two coexisting charge density waves with slightly mismatched wavevectors has been realized. These incommensurate charge density waves can collectively exhibit commensurability, forming a jointly commensurate charge density wave that provides a paradigm for controlling moiré potential and periodicity.

title: Page kidney in a solid-organ transplant recipient with acute renal failure and arterial hypertension
creator: Malissa Bentham, Nerissa Jurawan, Lisa Belle, Margaret O'Shea
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryPage kidney (Page phenomenon) is a rare and treatable cause of hypertension which can occur if a haematoma, leading to extrinsic compression, occurs after renal transplant biopsy. The renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system is activated leading to hypertension. This case report is that of a male in his 70s who had a renal transplant biopsy of his transplanted kidney and subsequently developed Page phenomenon as a result of an expanding haematoma. He developed elevated blood pressure (BP) along with a decrease in his renal function.

title: Efficient Hamiltonian, structure and trace distance learning of Gaussian states
creator: Marco Fanizza, Cambyse Rouzé, Daniel Stilck França
description: When learning descriptions of many-body quantum systems, assuming locality of interactions can dramatically reduce the required number of observations and computational time compared to unstructured approaches. In this work, we uncover an infinite-dimensional instance of this phenomenon, initiating the study of Hamiltonian learning for positive-temperature bosonic Gaussian states.

title: Practical synthesis of 3-Oxa/Aza-bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes from 3-Oxa/Aza[3.1.1]propellanes
creator: Qin Jiang, Jianyang Dong, Fang Lei, Yanfeng Han, Mingxin Li, Yilin Zhang, Juan Fan, Huaming Sun, Ting Li, Shuoyi Chen, Zhendan Chen, Dong Xue
description: While bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs) and bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) serve as established 3D bioisosteres for para- and meta-substituted benzenes, accessible via ring-opening of their corresponding propellanes, the integration of heteroatoms into these propellane scaffolds has remained elusive. Herein, we report the practical synthesis of 3-oxa/aza[3.1.1]propellanes, two heteroatom-containing analogues of propellane, from 1,5-diiodo-3-hetero-BCHeps. On this basis, radical-based transformations of 3-oxa/aza[3.1.

title: Evolving strategies for addressing CAR T-cell toxicities
creator: Alexander W. Rankin, Brynn B. Duncan, Cecily Allen, Sara K. Silbert, Nirali N. Shah
description: The field of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has grown from a fully experimental concept to now boasting a multitude of treatments including six FDA-approved products targeting various hematologic malignancies. Yet, along with their efficacy, these therapies come with side effects requiring timely and thoughtful interventions.

title: Erosive potential of children’s chewable vitamin supplements: An in vitro investigation
creator: Wannee Lertsooksawat, Yanisa Tanjaruphan, Thanawat Chaima, Thanawat Lerdpibulchai, Tanawan Wittayathawornwong, Chayada Teanchai, Rudee Surarit, Sivaporn Horsophonphong
description: Background. Chewable vitamins are dietary supplements in which vitamins are combined with a flavor that appeals to children. The acidic nature of some vitamins and some flavoring agents may cause dental erosion. We investigated the effect of children’s chewable vitamin supplements on the loss of minerals in teeth.Methods.

title: Colorimetric changes of zirconia-reinforced lithium disilicate with varied thicknesses under UV aging conditions
creator: AbdelRahman Moammad Abdelhameed, Hussein Ramadam Mohammed, Ahmad Mohammad Yousri El Kouedi
description: Background. Zirconia-reinforced lithium disilicate (ZLD) is a promising material for esthetic dental restorations due to its strength, translucency, and color stability. However, its durability under accelerated aging conditions needs further investigation. The present in vitro study evaluated the effect of UV accelerated aging on the translucency and color stability of ZLD at varying thicknesses, using IPS e.

title: Improving engagement with preconsult patient-reported outcome measures: A mixed-methods pilot study
creator: Chen He, Ying Shan Cheung, Jia Yi Chua, Qasrina Lim, Ellie Choi
description: egies to improve preconsult PROMs completion and explored broader implementational barriers in an outpatient dermatology setting. Within each clinic list, dermatology outpatients were individually randomized to either an intervention arm testing a specific messaging strategy or a control arm using a standard template. PROM completion rates were compared between groups and supplemented by qualitative interviews and observations.

title: Breast Milk Macronutrients and Child Growth and Neurodevelopment in a Lactation Cohort in Rural Bangladesh
creator: Krysten North, Sophie Driker, Rasheda Khanam, Salahuddin Ahmed, Chloe Andrews, Mandy B Belfort, Sara Cherkerzian, Nabidul H Chowdhury, Tarik Hasan, Sayedur Rahman, Unmesha Roy Paladhi, Amy Lopez Esteban, Carmen Monthe-Dreze, Fahmida Tofail, Abdullah Baqui, Sarbattama Sen, Anne CC Lee
description: BackgroundLimited data exist on the relationship between breast milk macronutrient/energy concentrations and child outcomes in settings with high maternal undernutrition.ObjectivesThis study aims to determine associations of breast milk macronutrient (protein, fat, carbohydrate) and energy concentrations with child growth and neurodevelopment.

title: A green square-wave voltammetric method for albendazole determination at a glassy carbon electrode: first use of ethanol as an environmentally friendly solvent
creator: Ümran Sofu, Sude Telli, Zehra Üstün, Ebru Çubuk Demiralay
description: A simple, sensitive square-wave voltammetric method was developed for the determination of albendazole at an unmodified glassy carbon electrode, employing ethanol for the first time as a green co-solvent in the electroanalytical assay of this compound. Optimum conditions were established as Britton–Robinson buffer (pH 2.0) containing 20% (v/v) ethanol.

title: Periductal Mastitis Occurring Among Hubble-Bubble Smokers: A Report of Two Cases and Literature Review
creator: Rami Yaghan, Nehad M Ayoub, Lamees R Yaghan, Abdulla I Mohamed
description: Periductal mastitis (PM) is a form of nonlactational mastitis. The clinical picture varies from mild periareolar inflammation to frank retroareolar abscess formation. A huge amount of literature is incriminating cigarette smoking as a major contributing factor to the etiology of PM, and cessation of smoking is essential for a successful treatment.

title: Posterior Osteophyte Resection from the Medial Femoral Condyle Increases Medial Gap of Extension and Mid-Flexion in Total Knee Arthroplasty
creator: Ji Hyun Ahn, Ki-Tae Park
description: BackgroundThe present study aimed to determine the effect of posterior osteophyte resection from the medial femoral condyle on the medial gap increase in varus osteoarthritis during posterior-stabilized total knee arthroplasty (TKA).MethodsOne hundred and eight cases of primary posterior-stabilized TKA for varus knee osteoarthritis were reviewed retrospectively.

title: Fatal Delayed Cardiac Tamponade Following Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: A Case Report
creator: Sylusha Gadipudi, Yashitha Chirumamilla, Philip J McDonald
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Catheter ablation procedure for symptomatic atrial fibrillation is an established treatment. Cardiac tamponade is one of the several complications associated with atrial fibrillation ablation. We present the case of a 60-year-old male with a past medical history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis, hypotension on midodrine, atrial fibrillation status post-ablation a week prior, and a cerebrovascular accident who presented to the emergency department with complaints of weakness, nausea, vomiting, confusion and some syncopal episodes for the past few days.

title: Comparative Effects of Acellular Dermal Matrix and Atelocollagen Injections in Intratendinous Partial-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Jae-Yoon Baek, Eun-Ji Yoon, Kyeong-Eon Kwon, Jong-Ho Kim
description: BackgroundThe purpose was to compare the functional and structural outcomes between injectable acellular dermal matrix (ADM) and atelocollagen in patients with intratendinous partial-thickness rotator cuff tears.MethodsFrom January 2020 to May 2021, 115 consecutive patients with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed intratendinous partial-thickness supraspinatus tears who met the inclusion criteria were retrospectively identified.

title: The Design of a Controlled-Release Polymer of a Phytopharmaceutical Agent: A Study on the Release in Different PH Environments Using the Ultrafiltration Technique
creator: Oscar G Marambio, Alejandro Muñoz, Rudy Martin-Trasancos, Julio Sánchez, Guadalupe del C Pizarro, Edina Rusen
description: A series of hydrophilic copolymers were prepared using 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) and itaconic acid (IA) from free radical polymerization at different feed monomer ratios using ammonium persulfate (APS) initiators in water at 70 °C. The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxy acetic acid (2,4-D) was grafted to Poly(HEMA-co-IA) by a condensation reaction.

title: Conservative Treatment with Adjunctive Use of Teriparatide for Periprosthetic Humeral Fractures after Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Report of 6 Cases
creator: Hyuk-Joon Sohn, Bum-Soon Park, Junkyung Hwang, Jong Pil Yoon, Jin-Young Bang, Chul-Hyun Cho
description: BackgroundPeriprosthetic humeral fractures (PPHFs) after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RTSA) are challenging complications, particularly in elderly patients with osteoporotic bone and multiple comorbidities. Although surgical treatment is commonly recommended for displaced fractures, conservative management may be preferable in high-risk patients. This study reports 6 cases of PPHF after RTSA successfully treated with conservative management incorporating adjunctive teriparatide therapy.

title: Susceptibility of Mouse Brain to MCMV Infection and Neuroinflammation During Ontogeny
creator: Fran Krstanović, Andrea Mihalić, Lucija Šakota, Berislav Lisnić, Stipan Jonjić, Ilija Brizić, Yuying Liang
description: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) rarely infects the brain following infection of adult individuals. However, the virus readily infects the brain during congenital HCMV (cHCMV) infection, frequently causing severe neurodevelopmental and neurological sequelae. Interestingly, although the incidence of cHCMV infection is 0.5–1%, the proportion of congenitally infected individuals in which the virus manages to gain access to the brain is unknown.

title: Increased Accuracy of Acetabular Cup Positioning with an Automatic Impaction Device in Total Hip Arthroplasty
creator: Hyeongmin Song, Chan Young Lee, Taek-Rim Yoon, Kyung-Soon Park
description: BackgroundTraditionally, cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) has been primarily performed using a manual technique involving a hammer and an impactor. During cup insertion into the acetabulum, the manual technique may cause temporary limitations in visualization, discrepancies in the applied force, and imbalances in the force vector. Recently, automatic impaction devices have been developed and adopted for cup insertion.

title: Heparin Resistance in Patients Receiving Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Review
creator: Tatyana Li, Azhar Zhailauova, Aidyn Kuanyshbek, Iwan Wachruschew, Shaimurat Tulegenov, Vitaliy Sazonov, Timur Kapyshev, Holger Thiele, Karim Bendjelid, Pranas Šerpytis, Robertas Stasys Samalavičius
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Heparin resistance (HR) in patients on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) exacerbates bleeding and thrombogenesis. Thus far, there is no universal definition of what this condition entails and no unified strategy for assessing heparin’s efficacy in ECMO patients. The most frequent discrepancy when it comes to defining HR is the difference in the reported doses: units per day (U/d) or per kilogram per hour (U/kg/h). Another disagreement arises with regard to the various methods of measuring unfractionated heparin (UFH) efficacy.

title: The seduction of the target: individualized hemodynamics and the limits of precision care after esophagectomy
creator: Laurence Weinberg
description: day. For that reason, the randomized trial by Hovgaard and colleagues, published recently in Anesthesiology, is directly relevant to thoracic practice (1). It asks a deceptively simple question: if blood pressure and cardiac output are measured more carefully, individualized more deliberately, and treated for longer, will patients undergoing esophagectomy experience fewer complications? The answer is sobering.

title: Blood biomarkers and penalized logistic regression for the prediction of complicated appendicitis in children: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Masanaga Matsumoto, Yohei Sanmoto, Kouji Masumoto
description: Background:Early preoperative identification of complicated appendicitis in children is important for risk stratification. Several blood biomarkers have been proposed for this purpose, but their performance has rarely been compared directly within the same cohort. We aimed to clarify their relative diagnostic performance and to determine whether combining laboratory parameters using an elastic-net model provides incremental diagnostic value.

title: Acute superior mesenteric artery syndrome in a young adult: case report
creator: Mohamad Khalife, Mohamad E. Haress, Riwa Deghaim, Mustapha El Lakis, Hadeel Ghaddar, Mustafa Saad El Masri
description: Introduction and importance:Superior mesenteric artery (SMA) syndrome is a rare condition (incidence of 0.013%–0.78%) that primarily affects young adults, resulting from duodenal compression between the SMA and the aorta following rapid weight loss and retroperitoneal fat pad depletion. Conservative management succeeds in 70–80% of cases; surgical intervention is required for refractory symptoms.

title: Pancreatic metastasis from gastric adenocarcinoma: a rare clinical entity and therapeutic challenges
creator: Maryem Ben Brahim, Ahmed Ben Mahmoud, Aida Khadhar, Amine Sebai, Youssef Chaker, Montasser Kacem
description: Introduction:Pancreatic metastases from gastric adenocarcinoma are exceptionally rare and often present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological features make differentiation from primary pancreatic tumors particularly difficult, underscoring the need for a multidisciplinary approach.Case presentation:We report the case of a 54-year-old man who was initially treated in 2023 for gastric antral adenocarcinoma with independent cells.

title: Utility of Simultaneous Left Atrial Strain–Volume Relationship During Passive Leg Lift to Identify Elevated Left Ventricular Filling Pressure—A Proof-of-Concept Study
creator: Ashwin Venkateshvaran, Urban Wiklund, Per Lindqvist, Thomas Lindow
description: Background: The assessment of left ventricular (LV) filling pressure in heart failure (HF) poses a diagnostic challenge, as HF patients may have normal LV filling pressures at rest but often display elevated LV filling pressures during exercise. Rapid preload increase during passive leg lift (PLL) may unmask HF in such challenging scenarios.

title: Laparoscopic resection of a low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm in a patient with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a case report
creator: Masaya Aizawa, Shingo Tsujinaka, Yoh Kitamura, Yuuri Hatsuzawa, Tomoya Miura, Toru Nakano
description: Introduction and importance:Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (AMNs) are rare, and preoperative diagnosis can be challenging, particularly when other abdominal cystic diseases coexist. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), which is characterized by multiple cystic formations, can complicate both differential diagnosis and surgical planning.

title: Smart Concrete Using Optical Sensors Based on Bragg Gratings Embedded in a Cementitious Mixture: Cure Monitoring and Beam Test
creator: Edson Souza, Pâmela Pinheiro, Felipe Coutinho, João Dias, Ronaldo Pilar, Maria José Pontes, Arnaldo Leal-Junior
description: Smart concrete is a structural element that can combine both sensing and structural capabilities. In addition, smart concrete can monitor the curing of concrete, positively impacting design and construction approaches. In concrete, if the curing process is not well developed, the structural element may develop cracks in this early stage due to shrinkage, decreasing structural mechanical strength.

title: Bilateral giant pulmonary hydatid cysts in a toddler presenting as severe pneumonia: a risk-adapted staged surgical approach
creator: Davood Salehi, Negin Rostamzadeh, Samin Rostamzadeh
description: Background:Pulmonary hydatid disease is common in endemic regions, yet bilateral giant cysts in toddlers are exceptionally rare and may mimic severe pneumonia. Their management is challenging, particularly in physiologically vulnerable children.Case presentation:We report a 32-month-old girl presenting with fever, progressive cough, and severe respiratory distress.

title: A Miniaturized and Ultra-Low-Power Wireless Multi-Parameter Monitoring System with Self-Powered Ability for Aircraft Smart Skin
creator: Chongqi Wang, Yu Wang, Wei Pu, Lei Qiu
description: The aircraft smart skin (ASS) with structural health monitoring capabilities is a promising technology. It enables the real-time acquisition of the aircraft’s structural health status and service environment, thereby improving the performance of the aircraft and ensuring the safety of its operation, which in turn reduces maintenance costs.

title: Frozen autograft–prosthesis composite reconstruction with total hip arthroplasty for proximal femoral osteosarcoma: a case report
creator: Viet Nhuan Ngo, Phuoc Hung Do, Quang Vinh Pham, Hoang Phu Nguyen, Ba Vu Dong Phan
description: Introduction and importance:Reconstruction after proximal femoral resection requires restoration of both a large osseous defect and stable hip joint function. Frozen autograft–prosthesis composite (FAPC) reconstruction using liquid nitrogen-treated autograft represents a viable biological option for this indication. We present a case of proximal femoral osteosarcoma managed with this technique.

title: Realisation of an Application Specific Multispectral Snapshot-Imaging System Based on Multi-Aperture-Technology and Multispectral Machine Learning Loops
creator: Lennard Wunsch, Martin Hubold, Rico Nestler, Gunther Notni, Jose Alberto Rabadan Borges, Julio Francisco Rufo Torres
description: Multispectral imaging (MSI) enables the acquisition of spatial and spectral image-based information in one process. Spectral scene information can be used to determine the characteristics of materials based on reflection or absorption and thus their material compositions. This work focuses on so-called multi aperture imaging, which enables a simultaneous capture (snapshot) of spectrally selective and spatially resolved scene information.

title: The influence of virtual reality on anxiety and pain in breast cancer patients: A systematic review☆
creator: Finta Isti Kundarti, T. Triwiyanto, Ira Titisari, Untung Sujianto, Anis Nurlaili, Zacky Firlana Azmi
description: BackgroundBreast cancer has a high incidence and remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide. Virtual reality (VR) based interventions have emerged as an effective new strategy to reduce psychological distress and improve physical wellbeing. This study aims to examine the effect of virtual reality on anxiety and pain in breast cancer patients.

title: Mayan Medicinal Plants Bignonia potosina and Thouinia paucidentata Demonstrate Anti-Infective Properties Against the Priority Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
creator: Gloria María Molina-Salinas, Angel Dzul-Beh, Andrés Humberto Uc-Cachón, Haziel Eleazar Dzib-Baak, Avel Adolfo González-Sánchez, Geovani Antonio Palma-Pech, Carlos Javier Quintal-Novelo
description: (1) Background: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CBRAB) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CBRPA) are critical and high-priority pathogens that require new therapeutic developments. Medicinal plants are valuable pharmaceutical resources. This study explored the anti-infective properties of Mayan plants, Bignonia potosina, and Thouinia paucidentata.

title: Anti-Inflammatory and Anticancer Effects of Kaurenoic Acid in Overcoming Radioresistance in Breast Cancer Radiotherapy
creator: Tae Woo Kim, Seong-Gyu Ko
description: Background/Objectives: Peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor γ (PPARγ) plays a key role in mediating anti-inflammatory and anticancer effects in the tumor microenvironment. Kaurenoic acid (KA), a diterpene compound isolated from Sphagneticola trilobata (L.) Pruski, has been demonstrated to exert anti-inflammatory, anticancer, and antihuman immunodeficiency virus effects.

title: The ethics-driven data governance framework for health-based AI (EDG-AI4H): an integrated approach for empowering explainable AI in health insurance risk prediction in Iran
creator: Rezvan Rahimi
description: PurposeThe digital transformation of health data has enabled predictive models in insurance. In Iran, the absence of an indigenous data governance framework integrating ethical, legal, and technical considerations poses serious risks to responsible AI development. This study aimed to design an ethics-driven data governance framework to empower Explainable AI (XAI) in health insurance risk prediction in Iran.

title: Exploring the Influence of Biochar-Supported Nano-Iron Oxide on Phosphorus Speciation Transformation and Bacterial Community Structure in Aerobic Pig Manure Composting Processes
creator: Ning Yuan, Kang Wang, Mengyue Liang, Jia Zhou, Rui Yu, Alexander Machado Cardoso
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Existing studies have demonstrated the positive effects of nano-sized iron oxide on compost maturity, yet the impact of nano-sized iron oxide on phosphorus speciation and bacterial communities during the composting process remains unclear. In this study, pig manure and straw were used as raw materials, with biochar-supported nano-sized iron oxide (BC-Fe3O4NPs) as an additive and calcium peroxide (CaO2) as a co-agent, to conduct an aerobic composting experiment with pig manure.

title: Effects of moisture content on the co-oxidation behavior of sturgeon myofibrillar protein and sturgeon oil
creator: Yizhou Fang, Zhengmei Yin, Jinshui Yu, Guangrong Huang, Junhui Li
description: This study systematically investigated the moisture-dependent regulation of marine protein–lipid co-oxidation across a broad moisture range (10–90%), with particular emphasis on the poorly understood intermediate-moisture region. Protein and lipid oxidation exhibited a non-linear response to increasing moisture content, first intensifying and then declining, with the most extensive co-oxidation observed at 70% MC.

title: Small Molecules in Parkinson’s Disease Therapy: From Dopamine Pathways to New Emerging Targets
creator: Hwayoung Lee, Ahmed Elkamhawy, Polina Rakhalskaya, Qili Lu, Hossam Nada, Guofeng Quan, Kyeong Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a chronic, progressive neurological disorder affecting approximately 10 million people worldwide, with prevalence expected to rise as the global population ages. It is characterized by the degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, leading to motor symptoms such as tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability, and gait disturbances, as well as non-motor symptoms including olfactory disturbances, sleep disorders, and depression. Currently, no cure exists for PD, and most available therapies focus on symptom alleviation.

title: Optimization of immune priming interval using Imuno-FS Plus enhances the efficacy of oral formalin-killed Vibrio parahaemolyticus vaccine in Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei)
creator: Annisa Widya Ananda, Sri Nuryati, Dinamella Wahjuningrum, Munti Yuhana, Ardana Kurniaji
description: Acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (AHPND), caused by toxigenic Vibrio parahaemolyticus, remains a major constraint in Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) aquaculture. This study evaluated whether the interval between adjuvant-induced immune priming and oral vaccination could be optimized to enhance the efficacy of a formalin-killed V. parahaemolyticus vaccine. Shrimp were fed a diet supplemented with Imuno-FS Plus powder (0.

title: Iridium-Catalyzed Highly Selective 1,4-Reduction of α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyl Compounds
creator: Youwei Chen, Jide Li, Jiaxi Xu, Zhanhui Yang
description: In this study, an iridium-catalyzed selective 1,4-reduction of α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds is realized, with water as a solvent and formic acid as a hydride donor. The new efficient iridium catalyst features a 2-(4,5-dihydroimidazol-2-yl)quinoline ligand. The chemoselectivity and catalyst efficiency are highly dependent on the electronic and steric properties of the substrates.

title: Thermal Performance Enhancement of a Biomimetic Fish-Fin Latent Heat Storage Unit Using CNTs-COOH/Erythritol Composite Phase Change Material
creator: Shiping Liu, Zhenggui Li, Baozhu Han, Yanxiong Jiao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Phase change energy storage is a key technology for mitigating the volatility and intermittency of renewable energy and plays an important role in improving the efficiency, stability, and reliability of energy systems. To enhance the thermal conductivity of erythritol (Ery), this study introduces carboxylated carbon nanotubes (CNTs-COOH) as a high-thermal-conductivity filler into the Ery matrix to prepare a composite phase change material (CPCM). Inspired by biomimetic principles, a biomimetic fish-fin latent heat storage structure was designed.

title: A Single Amino Acid in the A2 Linker of Cholera Toxin Affects the Efficiency of Toxin Disassembly and Resulting Toxicity
creator: Flore Kersten, Natalia Mojica, Albert Serrano, Joel B. Heim, Jessica L. Guyette, Henrique Musseli Cezar, Gabriele Cordara, Suren A. Tatulian, Michele Cascella, Ute Krengel, Ken Teter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cholera toxin (CT) from Vibrio cholerae and heat-labile enterotoxin (LT) from enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli are highly related AB5-type protein toxins that contain a catalytic A1 subunit, an A2 linker, and a cell-binding homopentamer of B subunits. The two proteins bind the same GM1 receptor and have similar levels of enzymatic activity toward their shared Gsα target, yet CT is more potent than LT.

title: Vibrational and DFT Studies and Anticancer Activity of Novel Pd(II) and Pt(II) Complexes with Chloro Derivatives of 7-Azaindole-3-Carbaldehyde
creator: Ksenia Szmigiel-Bakalarz, Dagmara Kłopotowska, Joanna Wietrzyk, Magdalena Malik, Barbara Morzyk-Ociepa, Ana Margarida Gomes da Silva
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study investigates the structural, vibrational, and biological properties of novel palladium(II) and platinum(II) complexes with 5-chloro-7-azaindole-3-carbaldehyde (5ClL) and 4-chloro-7-azaindole-3-carbaldehyde (4ClL) ligands. Infrared and Raman spectroscopy, combined with DFT (ωB97X-D) calculations, provided valuable information about metal–ligand interactions, the cis or trans conformation of the aldehyde group in the ligands, and the presence of trans isomers in the metal complexes obtained in the solid state.

title: Combination of Polymeric Microneedles with Specific Peptide for TNF‑α Sensing Via Noninvasive Detection in Interstitial Fluid
creator: Anna Palma, Concetta Di Natale, Daniele Tammaro, Elena Lagreca, Alessia Cugudda, Sara La Manna, Vincenzo Ferraro, Veronica Vespini, Simonetta Grilli, Pier Luca Maffettone, Sara Coppola
description: Microneedle (MN)-based biosensors offer a minimally invasive and blood-free approach for real-time monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers in interstitial fluid (ISF). Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α) can reach higher concentrations in ISF than in serum, which makes this fluid particularly sensitive for detecting early local inflammatory responses.

title: Nanocomposites Based on Iron Oxide and Carbonaceous Nanoparticles: From Synthesis to Their Biomedical Applications
creator: Mirela Văduva, Andreea Nila, Adelina Udrescu, Oana Cramariuc, Mihaela Baibarac
description: Nanocomposites based on Fe3O4 and carbonaceous nanoparticles (CNPs), including carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene derivatives (graphene oxide (GO) and reduced graphene oxide (RGO)), such as Fe3O4@GO, Fe3O4@RGO, and Fe3O4@CNT, have demonstrated considerable potential in a number of health applications, including tissue regeneration and innovative cancer treatments such as hyperthermia (HT).

title: Engineering Morphology and Dimensionality in 1D and 2D Cu(I)‑I Coordination Polymers for Enhanced Photocatalysis, Luminescence, and Selective Antibiotic Sensing
creator: Julian Avila-Duran, Carlos Tabernero-Sestines, Fernando Aguilar-Galindo, Pilar Amo-Ochoa
description: Copper­(I) iodide coordination polymers (CPs) based on pyridine- and pyrazine-derived ligands are luminescent materials typically synthesized under solvothermal conditions using organic solvents. Herein, the archetypal compounds [CuI­(4-methylpyridine)]n (CP1) and [Cu2I2(2-methylpyrazine)]n (CP2) were synthesized through one-step room-temperature methods, reducing the need for conventional high-temperature solvothermal procedures.

title: Experimental Study on the Flexural Performance of Composite Beams with Lipped Channels
creator: Changyong Lee, Byungho Bae, Seunghun Kim, Taesoo Kim, Yuri Ribakov
description: This study conducted experiments to investigate the flexural behavior of steel–concrete composite beams with U-shaped sections, utilizing cold-formed lipped channels as web components. To enhance both flexural and shear performance, trapezoidal plates were added to the lower sides of the composite beams.

title: Five-year implementation and longitudinal performance of a multidisciplinary acute myocardial infarction program in a middle-income country
creator: Beatriz Mantilla Pérez, Alexandra Hurtado-Ortiz, Paula Andrea Gualteros Cely, Juliet López Serrano, Anderson Bermon Angarita, Edgar Fabián Manrique-Hernández, Maricel Licht-Ardila, José Federico Saiibi
description: BackgroundAcute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of mortality in low- and middle-income countries, where delayed reperfusion worsens outcomes. Evidence on the long-term operation of multidisciplinary AMI programs in these settings is limited. We aimed to describe the five-year performance of a multidisciplinary AMI program in quality-of-care indicators and clinical outcomes.

title: Adaptive Control of Pressure Difference in Abrasive Flow Machining for Inner Hole with High Depth/Diameter Ratio
creator: Yaojie Cai, Panyu Qian, Donghui Wen, Guixiang Jin, Mingsheng Jin, Qiaoling Yuan, Li Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To address the issue of uneven pressure distribution in the abrasive flow field within the inner hole of components with a large depth/diameter ratio, an adaptive control strategy for regulating flow field pressure difference is proposed in this paper. The strategy was based on the effects of pressure fluctuations at the abrasive flow inlet and outlet on pressure distribution patterns and pressure changes within the inner hole flow field, as derived from numerical simulations.

title: Drosophila l(2)23CDe A8-1 and l(2)23CDf A18-2 are missense alleles of the SerRS gene
creator: Benjamin Galligos, Giovanna Caime, Alexis Michalski, Jamie Dyer
description: Viability requires that certain genes are expressed at the correct levels and at specific times during development. Many genes have already been determined as essential to development, but many more may exist. Numerous lethal mutations have been isolated in Drosophila melanogaster that have yet to be identified at the gene level.

title: Forming Control and Wear Behavior of M2 High-Speed Steel Produced by Direct Energy Deposition on Curved Surface
creator: Lan Jiang, Xiaofang Pan, Zhongkai Li, Bo Yuan, Wenxin Liu, Danya Li, Ge Shen, Jun Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Direct energy deposition (DED) technology shows promising applications in the production of roller die cutters. The optimization of process parameters, scanning strategies, and analyses of compressive properties and wear behavior are required prior to application. Therefore, this work investigated the influence of scanning strategy and overlap ratio on the microstructure, microhardness, compressive properties, and wear resistance of M2 high-speed steel (HSS) with DED on a 316 L cylindrical surface.

title: Bottom-Up Model Suggesting Membrane Localization of Heme Oxygenase‑1 Contributes to Heme Selection for Degradation
creator: Ryusei Matsutani, Yuka Kodama, Tomoichiro Kusumoto, Masakazu Sugishima, Hiroshi Sakamoto, Junichi Taira
description: Heme functions as a prosthetic group in numerous hemoproteins, whereas a fraction of intracellular heme is not tightly bound to proteins or membranes and can readily dissociate; this labile heme participates in the regulation of diverse cellular processes. Heme has pro-oxidant properties and is cytotoxic at elevated levels.

title: SlUPA-like, a bHLH Transcription Factor in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum), Serves as the Crosstalk of GA, JA and BR
creator: Pengyu Guo, Xin Cheng, Yunshu Wang, Guoping Chen, Xuqing Chen, Yingwu Yang, Xiuhai Zhang, Zongli Hu, Mario A Pagnotta
description: The bHLH (basic Helix–Loop–Helix) transcription factor serves as pivotal controller in plant growth and development. In a previous study, the overexpression of SlUPA-like in Solanum lycopersicum L. Ailsa Craig (AC++) altered the JA (Jasmonic acid) response and endogenous GA (Gibberellic acid) content. However, the detailed regulation mechanism was not fully explored.

title: Minimal residual disease and relapse surveillance in osteosarcoma: an action-linked framework integrating liquid biopsy and imaging biomarkers
creator: Guoli Huang, Yang Zhou, Hao Wang, Xiucai Ma
description: Osteosarcoma relapse surveillance remains dominated by scheduled imaging because salvage treatment depends on anatomical confirmation of pulmonary, local or extrapulmonary recurrence. However, radiological recurrence may occur after a biologically active phase in which residual viable disease or micrometastatic progression is already present but not yet localizable.

title: Special Issue: “Enzymes and Enzyme Inhibitors—Applications in Medicine and Diagnosis 2.0”
creator: Athina Geronikaki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). er(I) and gold(I) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes have been attracting attention because of their catalytic activities. The anticancer activity of these complexes was evaluated against two breast cancer cell lines, resulting in a higher activity towards triple-negative MDA-MB-231, where they induced DNA damage due to the inhibition of human topoisomerase I (hTopoI) [2] and also regulated NF-κB localization [2] and TNF-α protein levels [3].

title: Novel revertants of Chlamydomonas vfl2 suggest a role for a flexible central α-helical region in centrin function in flagellar basal bodies
creator: Takako Kato-Minoura, Ichiro Sasaki, Ritsu Kamiya
description: A Chlamydomonas mutant, vfl2 , displays aberrant flagellar numbers due to an E101K mutation in the centrin gene. We isolated 21 revertants–12 intragenic and 9 extragenic–that suppress the mutant's abnormal phenotype. AlphaFold2 modeling indicates that the wild-type, mutant, and revertant proteins are structurally similar.

title: Utilizing the Fungal Bicistronic System for Multi-Gene Expression to Generate Insect-Resistant and Herbicide-Tolerant Maize
creator: Yuxiao Chen, Wenjie Lv, Qun Yue, Ning Wen, Yinxiao Wang, Zhihong Lang, Wei Xu, Shengyan Li
description: Developing simple and efficient multi-gene expression systems is crucial for multi-trait improvement or bioproduction in transgenic plants. In previous research, an IGG6-based bicistronic system from the nonpathogenic fungus Glarea lozoyensis efficiently expressed multiple enzyme proteins in yeast and maize, and the heterologous enzymes successfully performed their catalytic activity to reconstruct the biosynthetic pathway in the host organism.

title: Mentha-mediated selenium nanoparticles attenuate adriamycin-induced chronic kidney disease via multi-target modulation of oxidative, inflammatory, and fibrotic pathways
creator: Ayman E Abdelaziz, Ahmed A Shokeir, Basem I Awad, Amira Awadalla, AM Abdelghany, Omali Y El-Khawaga
description: Highlights•Mentha-mediated SeNPs protect against Adriamycin-induced chronic kidney injury via multi-target molecular modulation.•Green-synthesized SeNPs restore renal function and preserve kidney histoarchitecture in CKD rats.•SeNPs reduce oxidative stress and suppress apoptosis by inhibiting Bax and p53 signaling pathways.•Anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic actions of SeNPs involve downregulation of TNF-α, TGF-β, Collagen, and α-SMA.•Biosynthesized SeNPs represent a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for chronic kidney disease management.

title: New Chemo-, Regio- and Stereoselective Reactions and Methods in Organic Synthesis
creator: Maxim V Musalov
description: um synthesis has opened up effective approaches to new classes of organoselenium compounds [1,2,3,4]. This area of organic chemistry based on these bifunctional electrophilic selenium reagents continues to develop actively. For example, selenium dihalides have made it possible to synthesize a number of 9-selenabicyclo[3.3.

title: Influence of postpartum disorders, parity, and season on estimated methane emissions in dairy cows in northwest of Spain
creator: J. Álvarez, A. Acción, R. Barrionuevo, U. Yáñez, J.J. Becerra, A.I. Peña, J. Cainzos, R. Fouz, L.Á. Quintela
description: Highlights•Warm-season cows had lower milk yield but higher methane intensity.•Multiparous cows emitted more methane overall, but less methane per unit of milk.•Methane intensity was the highest in early lactation.•Dairy herd improvement based methane estimates can assess herd emission efficiency.•Better transition health may lower methane intensity.

title: Long-Term Histological Evaluation of a Novel Dermal Template in the Treatment of Pediatric Burns
creator: Zeena Gerster-Barzanji, Vivienne Woodtli, Mira Klix, Thomas Biedermann, Clemens Schiestl, Kathrin Neuhaus, Melinda Farkas, Jivko Kamarachev, Daniel Rittirsch, Sophie Böttcher-Haberzeth
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). For pediatric patients with full-thickness burns, achieving adequate dermal regeneration is essential to prevent inelastic scars that may hinder growth. Traditional autologous split-thickness skin grafts alone often fail to restore the dermal layer adequately. This study evaluates the long-term effect of using a NovoSorb® Biodegradable Temporizing Matrix (BTM) as a dermal scaffold in four pediatric patients, promoting dermal formation before autografting.

title: Gluteal compartment syndrome following prolonged immobilization in the setting of polysubstance use: A two-patient case series
creator: Mark Gamadia, Robert Garner, Daulton Sauce, Molly Black
description: IntroductionGluteal compartment syndrome (GCS) is a rare, often overlooked emergency caused by rising compartment pressures leading to muscle and nerve ischemia, frequently after substance-related immobilization. Nonspecific symptoms such as diffuse pain and reduced mobility contribute to delayed diagnosis, increasing risk of irreversible neuromuscular injury and death.Case summaryTwo cases of GCS following polysubstance overdose are presented.

title: Exploring Beliefs, Concerns, Prenatal Care Advice, and Sources of Information About Gestational Weight Gain Among Immigrant Central American Pregnant Women in the United States
creator: Virginia A Moreno, Doris Lucero, Nachalie Rodriguez-Cruz, Qun Le, Mary L Greaney, Ana Cristina Lindsay, Paul B Tchounwou
description: Gestational weight gain (GWG) is critical for maternal and neonatal health, but excessive GWG can lead to complications such as gestational diabetes, hypertension, and increased obesity risk later in life. Minoritized and immigrant women often face higher risks of excessive GWG.

title: Reinterpretation of Conflicting ClinVar BRCA1 Missense Variants Using VarSome and CanVIG-UK Gene-Specific Guidance
creator: Min-Kyung So, Gaeul Jung, Hyun-Jeong Koh, Sholhui Park, Tae-Dong Jeong, Jungwon Huh, Gustavo Baldassarre
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The accurate interpretation of the BRCA1/2 variant is critical for diagnosing and treating hereditary breast and ovarian cancers. ClinVar is a widely used public database for genetic variants. Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity can occur when different submitters categorize the same genetic variant inconsistently as pathogenic (PV), likely pathogenic (LPV), likely benign (LBV), benign (BV), or a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). The conflicting ClinVar BRCA1/2 variant classifications hinder clinical decision making.

title: Role and Diagnostic Significance of Apolipoprotein D in Selected Neurodegenerative Disorders
creator: Agata Kolanek, Roman Cemaga, Mateusz Maciejczyk, Mario Plebani, Carlo Gabelli
description: The World Health Organization in 2021 ranked Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias as the seventh leading cause of death globally. Neurodegenerative disorders are progressive, intractable, and often fatal diseases. Early diagnosis may allow patients to enjoy prolonged survival with attenuated symptomatology because of early intervention. Hence, further research on finding non-invasive biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases is warranted.

title: Physical literacy: unlocking its inclusive potential in schools and beyond
creator: Myriam Bérubé, Margaux Hebinck, Marie Laberge, Claudia Verret, Annie Pouliot-Laforte
description: Physical literacy, originally developed within physical education settings to foster lasting engagement in physical activity, is increasingly recognized in Canada as a multidimensional framework encompassing physical, cognitive, and affective dimensions that support health and participation. Despite its inclusive intent, its implementation continues to face challenges related to equity, diversity, and social justice.

title: Alternative Non-Destructive Approach for Estimating Morphometric Measurements of Chicken Eggs from Tomographic Images with Computer Vision
creator: Jean Pierre Brik López Vargas, Katariny Lima de Abreu, Davi Duarte de Paula, Denis Henrique Pinheiro Salvadeo, Lilian Francisco Arantes de Souza, Carlos Bôa-Viagem Rabello, Zhengjun Qiu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The egg has natural barriers that prevent microbiological contamination and promote food safety. The use of non-destructive methods to obtain morphometric measurements of chicken eggs has the potential to replace traditional invasive techniques, offering greater efficiency and accuracy. This paper aims to demonstrate that estimates derived from non-invasive approaches, such as 3D computed tomography (CT) image analysis, can be comparable to conventional destructive methods.

title: Characterization of the Detailed Fatty Acid Profiles of a Large Number of Types of Cheese from the Mountains and Plains
creator: Giovanni Bittante, Nicolò Amalfitano, Franco Tagliapietra, Stefano Schiavon, Claudio Cipolat-Gotet, Giorgia Stocco, Rajka Božanić
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The aim of this study was to characterize the highly detailed fatty acid (FA) profiles of 258 cheeses of 18 different categories of cheese collected in the mountains and on the plains of the Veneto region (Italy).

title: Stochastic Model for a Piezoelectric Energy Harvester Driven by Broadband Vibrations
creator: Angelo Sanfelice, Luigi Costanzo, Alessandro Lo Schiavo, Alessandro Sarracino, Massimo Vitelli
description: We present an experimental and numerical study of a piezoelectric energy harvester driven by broadband vibrations. This device can extract power from random fluctuations and can be described by a stochastic model, based on an underdamped Langevin equation with white noise, which mimics the dynamics of the piezoelectric material.

title: In vitro pharmacological evaluation of the safety and antibacterial efficacy of a Chilean honey hydrogel for veterinary wound applications
creator: Andrea Julieta Müller-Sepúlveda, Liliam Monsalve, Carolina Campos-Estrada, Valeska Guevara-Torrejón, Ricardo Ceriani, Claudia Foerster
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionHoney-based biomaterials have gained increasing interest as topical strategies for wound-related applications because of their antimicrobial, antioxidant, and tissue-supportive properties. However, the direct use of raw honey is limited by its viscosity, variability, and lack of standardized delivery systems.

title: The Phenotype Changes of Astrocyte During Different Ischemia Conditions
creator: Fei Meng, Jing Cui, Peng Wang, Junhui Wang, Jing Sun, Liang Li
description: Objectives: Dementia is becoming a major health problem in the world, and chronic brain ischemia is an established important risk factor in predisposing this disease. Astrocytes, as one major part of the blood–brain barrier (BBB), are activated during chronic cerebral blood flow hypoperfusion. Reactive astrocytes have been classified into phenotype pro-inflammatory type A1 or neuroprotective type A2.

title: Rehabilitation and therapeutic exercise in obstructive sleep apnea: a perspective beyond the apnea–hypopnea index
creator: Luis F. Guerrero-Vega, Víctor R. Jáuregui-Gutiérrez, Jonathan Elías-León, David A. Trejo-Osorio, Orlando R. Pérez-Nieto, Jonathan Reyes-Montufar, María del Carmen García-Pantoja, Fernando Mendiola-Enriquez, Cesar E. Vargas-Reynoso, Rafael A. Reyes-Monge, Silvana Macarena-Liendro, Mariana I. Razo-Alv
description: IntroductionObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a multisystem disease whose clinical impact extends beyond nocturnal respiratory events. Although the apnea hypopnea index (AHI) is widely used to classify disease severity, this parameter does not adequately reflect the functional, symptomatic, and quality-of-life burden experienced by individuals with OSA.

title: A Normative Model Representing Autistic Individuals Amidst Autism Spectrum Phenotypic Heterogeneity
creator: Joana Portolese, Catarina Santos Gomes, Vinicius Daguano Gastaldi, Cristiane Silvestre Paula, Sheila C. Caetano, Daniela Bordini, Décio Brunoni, Jair de Jesus Mari, Ricardo Z. N. Vêncio, Helena Brentani
description: Background: Currently, there is a need for approaches to understand and manage the multidimensional autism spectrum and quantify its heterogeneity. The diagnosis is based on behaviors observed in two key dimensions, social communication and repetitive, restricted behaviors, alongside the identification of required support levels.

title: Core–Shell PLGA Nanoparticles: In Vitro Evaluation of System Integrity
creator: Tatyana Kovshova, Julia Malinovskaya, Julia Kotova, Marina Gorshkova, Lyudmila Vanchugova, Nadezhda Osipova, Pavel Melnikov, Veronika Vadekhina, Alexey Nikitin, Yulia Ermolenko, Svetlana Gelperina, Il Je Yu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The objective of this study was to compare the properties of core–shell nanoparticles with a PLGA core and shells composed of different types of polymers, focusing on their structural integrity. The core PLGA nanoparticles were prepared either through a high-pressure homogenization–solvent evaporation technique or nanoprecipitation, using poloxamer 188 (P188), a copolymer of divinyl ether with maleic anhydride (DIVEMA), and human serum albumin (HSA) as the shell-forming polymers. The shells were formed through adsorption, interfacial embedding, or conjugation.

title: Impact of Removing the Monitoring Requirements for Holdings with Atypical Scrapie in Great Britain
creator: Mark Arnold, Bryony Jones, Verity Horigan, Robin Simons, Brenda Rajanayagam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryAtypical scrapie (AS) is a disease of sheep and goats. Currently, when AS is detected on a farm in Great Britain (GB), all animals that exit the flock through natural death or slaughter are tested for AS for a period of 2 years following detection of the initial case, as used to be performed within the European Union (EU), in order to provide support as to whether AS can transmit directly between sheep.

title: Pathological and Immunohistochemical Characterization of Follicular Gastritis (Gastric Lymphofollicular Hyperplasia) in 41 Dogs
creator: Andrada Negoescu, Corina Toma, Claudiu Gal, Constantin Ifteme, Bianca Bofan, Teodoru Soare, Irina Amorim, Raluca Maria Pop, Ştefan Cristian Vesa, Dragoș Hodor, Elvira Gagniuc, Cornel Cătoi, Marian Taulescu
description: Simple SummaryThis study of the gastric mucosa biopsies of 41 dogs highlighted the endoscopic, histopathological, and immunohistochemical findings of gastric lymphofollicular hyperplasia (GLFH), emphasizing its frequent occurrence in young French Bulldogs (75.06%). GLFH was associated with glandular atrophy, lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, fibrosis, and varying degrees of Helicobacter-like organisms (HLOs) colonization.

title: Season-specific nitrogen management shapes soil microbial communities and crop productivity in wheat–maize rotation system
creator: Mengru Xue, Wenyang Li, Haosen Wei, Zerong Wang, Baojin Guo, Chuangyun Wang, Peng Zhou, Fei Gao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Based on a long-term positioned field experiment in a wheat-maize double-cropping system, the regulatory mechanisms of nitrogen fertilizer legacy on soil-crop coordination and microbial functions remain unclear. A two-year field experiment was conducted with four treatments: CK: no N fertilizer applied during either wheat or maize seasons; W1M0: N carryover only during the winter wheat season; W0M1: N carryover only during the summer maize season; W1M1: N carryover during both wheat and maize seasons.

title: Aerobic Exercise Improves Cognitive Recovery in Mice with Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion by Modulating the Annexin-A1-MAPK Axis and Astrocyte Polarization
creator: Wei Zhang, Jing He, Yuxin Wang, Xiaozhen Wang, He Jin, Xu Zhang, Ling Kong, Yanchuan Wu, Yong Yang, Rong Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID), resulting from chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, represent the second most prevalent form of dementia globally. Aerobic exercise is widely acknowledged as an effective intervention for various cognitive disorders. This study utilized a bilateral common carotid artery stenosis (BCAS) model to investigate whether aerobic exercise promotes cognitive recovery through the Annexin-A1 (ANXA1)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) axis in BCAS mice.

title: Severe pre-treatment attrition in the care cascade: clinical outcomes and risk factors among older MDR/RR-TB patients in China
creator: Fangjing Zhou, Shanshan Huang, Huiying Feng, Jianwei Li, Huizhong Wu, Yuhui Chen, Wenpei Wen, Lebin Liu
description: BackgroundThe rising global burden of multidrug- and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) coincides with rapid population aging. Older patients face unique challenges, yet age-stratified analyses of the MDR/RR-TB care cascade are lacking, obscuring the specific barriers they encounter.ObjectiveThis study aimed to characterize the treatment cascade and identify factors associated with attrition among older MDR/RR-TB patients in China.

title: Laser-Induced Graphene Electrodes for Flexible pH Sensors
creator: Giulia Massaglia, Giacomo Spisni, Tommaso Serra, Marzia Quaglio, Francesco Ruffino, Antonino Scandurra
description: In the growing field of personalized medicine, non-invasive wearable devices and sensors are valuable diagnostic tools for the real-time monitoring of physiological and biokinetic signals. Among all the possible multiple (bio)-entities, pH is important in defining health-related biological information, since its variations or alterations can be considered the cause or the effect of disease and disfunction within a biological system.

title: Short-term efficacy and safety of CO2 laser vaporization for anal intraepithelial neoplasia
creator: Tingting Su, Yi Yu, Fang Chen, Hongwei Zhang, Lu Zhang, Qing Cong, Long Sui, Limei Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the short-term efficacy, safety, and human papillomavirus (HPV) clearance outcomes of carbon dioxide (CO2) laser vaporization in patients with anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN), and to identify independent predictors of persistent postoperative HPV infection.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted on 99 patients who underwent CO2 laser ablation for AIN at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University between October 2023 and October 2024. Patients were categorized into four groups based on lesion location (perianal vs.

title: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici Exhibited a Significant Change in Virulence and Race Frequency in Xinjiang, China
creator: Hong Yang, Muhammad Awais, Feifei Deng, Li Li, Jinbiao Ma, Guangkuo Li, Kemei Li, Haifeng Gao, Dongfang Ma
description: Xinjiang is an important region due to its unique epidemic characteristics of wheat stripe rust disease caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici. Some previous studies on race identification were conducted in this region, but it is still unclear how temporal changes affect the dynamics, diversity, and virulence characteristics of Pst races in Xinjiang.

title: Comparative Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation on Oxidative Stress in Relapsing–Remitting Multiple Sclerosis
creator: Martyna Lis, Natalia Niedziela, Jowita Adamczyk-Zostawa, Jolanta Zalejska-Fiolka, Jarosław Szczygieł, Agata Sowa, Agata Świętek, Monika Adamczyk-Sowa, Arumugam R Jayakumar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Studies suggest that vitamin D (VitD) may reduce oxidative stress (OS) in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients. This study aimed to compare the effects of various VitD doses on OS in relapsing–remitting MS (RRMS). A 6-month supplementation was introduced using two doses of VitD: 2000 IU/day in the high-dose group (HD, n = 23) and 15,960 IU/month in the low-dose group (LD, n = 29). Significant differences in body weight, height, and age were found between groups.

title: A cross-sectional evaluation of large language model chatbot interfaces for patient-facing herpes zoster information: safety, information quality, and readability
creator: Dalian Liang, Cong Mai, Zhengkun Zhang, Jieyun Lin, Xianmei Wu, Haiying Lu, Jingli Shang, Huajun Wang, Haiyan Li
description: BackgroundLarge language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to obtain health information. However, fluent and clinically plausible responses may still contain safety-relevant omissions, inadequate source attribution and disclosure, or difficult-to-read text.ObjectiveTo evaluate the safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, response-level source attribution and disclosure, overall quality, and readability of five LLM chatbot interfaces answering lay-oriented questions about herpes zoster.

title: An Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition Using Multi-Class CSP
creator: Behzad Yousefipour, Vahid Rajabpour, Hamidreza Abdoljabbari, Sobhan Sheykhivand, Sebelan Danishvar
description: In recent years, significant advancements have been made in the field of brain–computer interfaces (BCIs), particularly in the area of emotion recognition using EEG signals. The majority of earlier research in this field has missed the spatial–temporal characteristics of EEG signals, which are critical for accurate emotion recognition.

title: Clinical characteristics of pulmonary nocardiosis in patients with and without bronchiectasis: a single-center retrospective comparative study
creator: Songsong Yu, Zhenru Ma, Kun Yang, Qianyu Zhang, Qiuhong Fang
description: BackgroundBronchiectasis is a common structural lung disease associated with pulmonary nocardiosis (PN), but the differences between PN patients with and without bronchiectasis remain insufficiently characterized.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective study of hospitalized patients with PN at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital from January 2012 to December 2024. Patients were grouped by bronchiectasis status, and their clinical, radiological, and microbiological features were compared.

title: Preparation of Chitosan Oleogel from Capillary Suspension and Its Application in Pork Meatballs
creator: Shishuai Wang, Zhongqin Fan, Xinya Huang, Yue Gao, Hongwei Sui, Jun Yang, Bin Li
description: In the oil dispersion of chitosan, the formation of a capillary bridge was triggered by adding a small amount of water to obtain an oleogel. With this method, the types of liquid oil and the ratio of oil/chitosan/water were explored to achieve an optimal oleogel. MCT performed best, followed by soybean oil, which was chosen for its edibility and cost.

title: Psychosocial transformation in women new to fitness: a phenomenological study on body image, self-confidence, and identity construction
creator: Mehdi Duyan, Gamze Ok, Ilker Gunel, Mehmet Bayansalduz, Vlad Adrian Geantă
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionDespite the increase in gym memberships in recent years, women’s participation in physical activity continues to lag behind men’s. Studies that holistically address the experiences of women newly starting fitness are limited in the literature.

title: C-X-C Motif Chemokine 12 Was Identified as a Potential Gene Target in the Treatment of Crohn’s Disease
creator: Hongsai Hu, Rong He, Minji Liu, Hongbing Zhou, Lin Tan, Qiongjia Ai, Qian Wang, Luwei Zeng, Weiming Qu
description: ObjectThe present study aimed to identify hub genes associated with the treatment and control of active and inactive Crohn’s disease (CD).MethodsDifferentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in normal, active CD, and inactive CD samples from GSE95095 dataset. Intersection genes screened by Venn diagram in DEGs.

title: Patient Safety Climate in Danish Primary Care: Adaption and Validation of the Danish Safety Attitudes Questionnaire (SAQ-DK-PRIM) [Response to Letter]
creator: Marie Haase Juhl, Anne Estrup Olesen, Ellen Tveter Deilkås, Niels Henrik Bruun, Kirsten Høgh Obling, Nikoline Rytter, Maya Damgaard Larsen, Solvejg Kristensen
description: Safety Attitudes Questionnaire (SAQ-DK-PRIM)” by Juhl et al.1 We are very happy for the in-depth interest in the topic of patient safety culture, the study and the article. We value the kind and professional recommendations for potential areas for further consideration received from Tien Zubaidah and Norlaila Sofia in Indonesia.

title: Long-Term Outcome of Childhood Asthma: Characterizing COPD-A and COPD-C Subtypes in Adulthood
creator: Osman Savran, Klaus Bønnelykke, Charlotte Suppli Ulrik
description: Background and AimAsthma in early life has been linked to subsequent development of COPD and according to GOLD 2023 COPD may be divided into distinct subtypes. We aimed to investigate factors associated with the GOLD classification COPD-A (asthma in childhood) and COPD-C (tobacco exposure) in a cohort of adults with a history of severe childhood asthma.

title: The potential role and research progress of the gut microbiota–NGF axis in postmenopausal bone homeostasis imbalance
creator: Yangyang Chen, Dingpeng Li, Zhong Wang, Jiawen Li, Haoze Zhang, Xingwen Xie
description: Postmenopausal osteoporosis(PMOP)is a common metabolic bone disease characterized by an imbalance in bone remodeling due to estrogen deficiency. Increasing evidence suggests that alterations in gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, immune response, microbial metabolites, and autonomic nervous activity are involved in postmenopausal bone loss.

title: Integrative Proteomics and Phosphoproteomics Profiling of Symptomatic Accessory Navicular Bone Based on Tandem Mass Tag Technology
creator: Bin Liu, Ran Wei, Yuqing Wang, Zishen Cheng, Liangliang Jiang, Xiaopeng Pu, Yaxing Zhang, Yantao Wang, Qiangjun Kang
description: BackgroundThe accessory navicular bone (ANB) is a common accessory bone in the foot. Certain ANBs significantly impair patients’ feet normal walking function. Foot injury is associated with ANB after athletic training. However, the molecular mechanism of foot injury with ANB after athletic training remains unclear.

title: Effects of blood flow restriction combined with interval training on aerobic capacity, anaerobic performance, and sport-specific performance in trained male athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Jingyu Shen, Dan Wu, Liye Liu
description: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of blood flow restriction (BFR) combined with interval training on aerobic capacity, anaerobic performance, and sport-specific performance in trained male athletes. We searched Cochrane Library, SPORTDiscus via EBSCO, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to 15 May 2026.

title: Emergency cesarean delivery followed by extended left hepatectomy and right hepatic hemangioma enucleation for giant hepatic hemangioma with intratumoral hemorrhage in late pregnancy: a case report
creator: Yuting Xiao, Honghui Zhang, Weiming Yi, Chao Guo, Ting Dai, Chuang Peng, Xinli Zhang, Dan Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Management of giant hepatic hemangioma (HH) complicated by intratumoral hemorrhage in late pregnancy is rarely reported and remains particularly challenging because maternal hemorrhagic compromise and fetal safety must be addressed simultaneously. We report the case of a 36-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman at 33 weeks and 5 days of gestation who was admitted after a heterogeneous abdominal mass was detected on routine prenatal ultrasonography.

title: Nomogram for Predicting in-Hospital Severe Complications in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Admitted in Emergency Department
creator: Yaqin Song, Kongzhi Yang, Yingjie Su, Kun Song, Ning Ding
description: BackgroundThere is lack of predictive models for the risk of severe complications during hospitalization in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). In this study, we aimed to create a nomogram to forecast the likelihood of in-hospital severe complications in AMI.

title: The Predictive Value of Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index in Patients with Granulomatous Mastitis
creator: Liquan Ouyang, Jieting Qin, Tianyue Cui, Yuyan Tan
description: PurposeThe systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) comprehensively reflects the balance between immune status and host inflammation. We aimed to investigate the potential predictive value of the SII in the prognosis of granulomatous mastitis (GM).Patients and MethodsWe enrolled 245 patients with GM who underwent surgery between 2015 and 2020 in this study.

title: Thrombotic Risk Assessment, P-Selectin, and Thromboprophylaxis Use Among, Cancer Patients at the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital, Calabar
creator: Kingsley Akaba, Edakabasi Akaba, Olukayode Oshatuyi, Brian Ssenkumba
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundVenous thromboembolism is the second leading cause of mortality among cancer patients. The Khorana Risk Assessment Score (KRAS) is widely acknowledged as the most validated tool in this context.AimTo assess the thrombotic risk in cancer patients using the modified Khorana Risk Assessment Score, examine the association between modified KRAS and soluble P-selectin levels, and document the utilization of thromboprophylaxis among cancer patients at the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital.MethodsThis was a cross-sectional hospital-based recruiting 100 cancer patients.

title: Nutritional status and weight trajectories during radiotherapy in patients with cancer: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Tong Liu, Shijin Wu
description: BackgroundPatients receiving radiotherapy are frequently malnourished, and weight loss can negatively impact treatment tolerance and clinical outcomes.ObjectiveThis retrospective cohort study aimed to assess nutritional status, weight trajectories, and changes in the prognostic nutritional index (PNI) over time, during radiotherapy.MethodologyThe medical records of 680 adult patients who initiated radiotherapy were reviewed retrospectively at a tertiary oncology center from 2023 to 2025.

title: In Reference to Primary site surgical resection in cM1 oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma
creator: Erkan Topkan, Efsun Somay, Uğur Selek
description: eated with chemotherapy (CT), chemoradiotherapy (CRT), surgical resection + adjuvant chemotherapy (S‐CT), and surgical resection + adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (S‐CRT), respectively. Respective 5‐year OS rates were 9.4%, 15.2%, 8.3%, and 23.8% (p < .001), indicating that surgical resection was beneficial only when combined with CRT.

title: Complex venous access in superior vena cava syndrome secondary to gray zone lymphoma, case report
creator: Martin Razus, Maros Kunderlik, Michal Marko, Vanda Repiska, Pavol Povinec, Bela Mrinakova
description: IntroductionMediastinal gray zone lymphoma (MGZL) is a rare and biologically complex lymphoma with overlapping features of primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma and classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Bulky mediastinal disease frequently complicates central venous access, particularly in the presence of superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome. Reports addressing optimal vascular access strategies in this setting remain limited.

title: Factors Influencing Presenteeism in Middle-aged and Older Workers with Chronic Kidney Disease: A Single-center Cross-sectional Study
creator: Aki Tabata, Hiroki Yabe, Takehide Katogi, Yuya Mitake, Shunta Oono, Tomoya Yamaguchi, Takayuki Fujii
description: Objectives:Managing presenteeism among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is important for balancing disease management and employment. This study aimed to investigate presenteeism, exercise self-efficacy (SE), and physical function indices in workers with CKD and to examine the factors that influence presenteeism in this patient group.Methods:This cross-sectional study included 36 workers with stage 3–5 pre-dialysis CKD.

title: Editorial: Rising stars in nephrology 2024: illuminating the future of kidney health
creator: Peter Kotanko
description: s conceived to give early-career investigators a platform to present their original research, reviews, and clinical perspectives that push the field forward, and its eleven contributions span the full spectrum of nephrology: nephron physiology and disease staging, pregnancy-related electrolyte disorders, pharmacotherapy for progressive CKD, cardiovascular risk after transplantation, biomarkers of acute and chronic kidney injury, the burden of immunosuppressive treatment,

title: Addressing Physical Inactivity in Mexican Children: The Role of Parents and Their Physical Literacy
creator: Nina Eisenburger, Edtna Jáuregui Ulloa, Cinthia Veronica Villegas Balderrama, Karen Janeth Villegas Balderrama, Sayra Nataly Muñoz Rodríguez, Alicia Calderón Escalante, Salvador Jesús López Alonso, Alejandra Orona Escápite, Luis Alberto Flores Olivares, Marisol Muñoz De la Riva, Tobias‐Jorge Kunde,
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionChildhood obesity and physical inactivity rates in Mexico are among the highest in the world. While parenting is a key factor in shaping children's physical activity behavior, there is a lack of research in this area, particularly in Mexico.ObjectiveThis qualitative study aims to better understand aspects of parenting relevant to children's physical engagement, including what parents understand by physical activity, how engaged they are and how important they find it, that is, their physical literacy.MethodsSeven focus group discussions were conducted with 43

title: Case Report: Acute prostatic swelling following hydrogel spacer insertion managed by MR-guided online adaptive radiotherapy
creator: Yushi Takahashi, Noriyoshi Takahashi, Sakiko Kageyama, Shohei Tanaka, Rei Umezawa, Takaya Yamamoto, Yu Suzuki, Keita Kishida, So Omata, Keiichi Jingu
description: BackgroundHydrogel spacers are widely used in radiotherapy for localized prostate cancer to reduce the rectal dose. While generally safe, acute anatomical changes in the prostate gland itself, specifically significant swelling, are poorly described and can compromise the precision of radiotherapy.Case presentationWe report a case of a 62-year-old man with high-risk prostate cancer (PSA 15.

title: Root-inspired, template-confined additive printing for fabricating high-robust conformal electronics
creator: Guifang Liu, Xiangming Li, Yangfan Qiu, Chuanhang Zeng, Xinkai Zhu, Chao Wang, Xiaoliang Chen, Chunhui Wang, Hongmiao Tian, Jinyou Shao
description: Conformal electronic devices on freeform surface play a critical role in the emerging smart robotics, smart skins, and integrated sensing systems. However, their functional structures such as circuits tend to tear-off, break, or crack under mechanical or thermal influence when in service, thus limiting the application reliability of conformal electronics.

title: Medication Changes After Renal Denervation: Current Evidence and Patient Perspectives
creator: Zhipeng Zhang, Fei Zhao, Runyu Ye, Xin Zhang, Yong Peng, Xiaoping Chen, Kai Liu
description: Renal denervation (RDN) is recognized as an adjunct therapy for hypertension management with a favorable and consistent blood pressure–lowering efficacy and safety profile. Alteration in medication burden is another noteworthy outcome of RDN for clinicians and patients. In this review, we summarized current clinical trials and patient perspectives, focusing on the use of antihypertensive medication (AHM) after RDN.

title: Comparative Efficacy of Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy vs Traditional Surgery in Lumbar Degenerative Disorders
creator: Zi-Kun Liao, Shu-Yang Xia, Qun Li, Wei Zhou, Ping Zhang
description: BackgroundLumbar degenerative diseases, such as lumbar disc herniation, cause significant pain and neurological deficits. Traditional surgeries like posteriior lumbar interbody fusion (PLIF) have drawbacks, including extensive tissue damage. We sought to evaluate the efficacy of unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) compared with PLIF, with a focus on clinical outcomes and complication rates.

title: Examining the impact of obstructive sleep apnea on cognitive function in severe COPD
creator: Kristina Kock Hansen, Anders Løkke, Hanne Irene Jensen, Eline Kirstine Gantzhorn, Ingeborg Farver-Vestergaard, Ole Hilberg
description: PurposeThis study aimed to examine the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and cognitive function in patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).MethodsPatients with severe COPD, who had not previously been diagnosed with OSA, were recruited between January 2021 and January 2023.

title: Assessment of the pterygoid hamulus dimensions and morphology in Iranian women using cone-beam computed tomography
creator: Zahra Mahdavi, Ladan Hafezi
description: Background. Understanding the characteristics of the pterygoid hamulus (PH) is crucial for diagnosing and treating various oropharyngeal and craniofacial conditions. It also aids in interpreting radiographs and diagnosing unexplained oropharyngeal pains. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is a valuable tool, offering clinical insights into this previously understudied area.

title: Effect of different bleaching protocols on the color and translucency parameters of a new monochromatic universal composite resin
creator: Mohammad Esmaeel Ebrahimi Chaharom, Mahmoud Bahari, Soodabeh Kimyai, Helia Bagban Nikzad
description: Background. Considering the few studies on the effect of bleaching protocols on the color properties of a newly developed monochromatic universal composite resin, the present study evaluated the effect of different bleaching protocols on the color change and translucency of Omnichroma (OMN) composite resin. Methods.

title: Association between the alkaline phosphatase-to-albumin ratio and recorded early all-cause mortality within 90 days of admission in patients with heart failure: a retrospective cohort study in a Chinese population
creator: Zhenyu Yuan, Mohan Li, Lei Zhao, Hong Geng, Qiang Ji, Kun Zuo, Yuanzhi Luo, Guanli Liang, Gengxu He
description: BackgroundAPAR combines alkaline phosphatase and albumin, two routine laboratory measurements. We examined its association with recorded early all-cause mortality within 90 days of admission in hospitalized patients with heart failure (HF), prioritizing continuous APAR over a mortality-derived cutoff.MethodsWe analyzed version 1.3 of the Zigong Heart Failure Database.

title: Development of the brain network control theory and its implications
creator: Zhoukang Wu, Liangjiecheng Huang, Min Wang, Xiaosong He
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Brain network control theory (NCT) is a groundbreaking field in neuroscience that employs system engineering and cybernetics principles to elucidate and manipulate brain dynamics. This review examined the development and applications of NCT over the past decade. We highlighted how NCT has been effectively utilized to model brain dynamics, offering new insights into cognitive control, brain development, the pathophysiology of neurological and psychiatric disorders, and neuromodulation. Additionally, we summarized the practical implementation of NCT using the nctpy package.

title: Positive narrative writing reduces music performance anxiety more effectively than traumatic narrative
creator: Xiaofen Song
description: Music performance anxiety (MPA) is a multidimensional construct that may impair performance quality and mental health, depending on individual and contextual factors. Current interventions are often costly, require specialized expertise, or lack feasibility. Expressive writing intervention (EWI) is low-cost and easy to implement.

title: Development and preliminary validation of a fertility concept scale for Chinese post-00s college students based on thematic analysis
creator: Lei Xiao, Xinrui Xiao, Zeyu Chen, Caihua Zhu, Yingmin Wu
description: BackgroundChina faces an increasingly acute risk of entering a “low-fertility trap,” and existing policy incentives have not produced the expected effects, underscoring the need to examine the micro-level psychological processes underlying fertility decision-making. Analyzing the fertility concepts of the post-00s generation is critical for predicting fertility behavior and informing targeted policies; however, suitable measurement tools remain lacking.

title: Effect of systematic nursing intervention on perioperative ocular symptoms in refractive surgery patients: evaluation using the ocular surface disease index scale
creator: Yidi Zhang, Ping Zhang, Ran Zhu, Xiumei Wu, Jincui Wei
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effect of systematic nursing intervention on perioperative ocular symptoms in patients undergoing femtosecond laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK), using the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) scale.MethodsA prospective case-control study was conducted including 69 patients (137 eyes) who underwent FS-LASIK between September 2023 and June 2024.

title: Investigating the Impact of Polymers on Clay Flocculation and Residual Oil Behaviour Using a 2.5D Model
creator: Xianda Sun, Yuchen Wang, Qiansong Guo, Zhaozhuo Ouyang, Chengwu Xu, Yangdong Cao, Tao Liu, Wenjun Ma, Alexander Malkin, Maria Graça Rasteiro
description: In the process of oilfield development, the surfactant–polymer (SP) composite system has shown significant effects in enhancing oil recovery (EOR) due to its excellent interfacial activity and viscoelastic properties. However, with the continuous increase in the volume of composite flooding injection, a decline in injection–production capacity (I/P capacity) has been observed.

title: Development of Antimicrobial Blends of Bacteria Nanocellulose Derived from Plastic Waste and Polyhydroxybutyrate Enhanced with Essential Oils
creator: Everton Henrique Da Silva Pereira, Marija Nicevic, Eduardo Lanzagorta Garcia, Vicente Fróes Moritz, Zeliha Ece Ozcelik, Buket Alkan Tas, Margaret Brennan Fournet, Carmen-Mihaela Popescu, Anamaria Irimia
description: The escalating global concern regarding plastic waste accumulation and its detrimental environmental impact has driven the exploration of sustainable alternatives to conventional petroleum-based plastics. This study investigates the development of antimicrobial blends of bacterial nanocellulose (BNC) derived from plastic waste and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHB), further enhanced with essential oils.

title: Divergent pathways from body image to disordered eating and physical activity: differential roles of thin-ideal and muscular-ideal internalization among Chinese female college students
creator: Hongquan Chen, Qian Li, Hanru Li, Han Liu, Hongyao Li, Yitong Wang, Jiaqi Xue, Meng Wang
